questions.question: When a stop is required at an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, what should a driver do?

options.text: They do not have to stop.
They should slow down to check that crossing traffic is clear.
They should stop where they can see 200 feet in both directions, even if they must enter the intersection.
They should stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should stop where they can clearly see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the point closest to the intersection where you can see approaching traffic clearly. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: What should you do before leaving an interstate highway?

options.text: Signal and move into the correct lane at least one mile before your exit.
Slow down to 45 miles per hour before reaching your exit.
Signal and slow down 50 to 100 feet before entering the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and move into the correct lane at least one mile before your exit.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and watch for exit signs. Move into the correct lane at least one mile before your exit. Do not slow down until after you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows the direction of a sharp curve in the road. The arrow points left, so the road curves sharply to the left. You may see several of these signs placed throughout the curve.

questions.question: What is important to do before turning left?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a yellow traffic light and have not yet entered it. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light, prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it quickly and safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Fire station ahead.
T intersection ahead.
Left turn signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for road conditions and hazards. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to respond to red, yellow, and green lights and to cross traffic.

questions.question: When a vehicle coming toward you is using high beams, you should look toward the ____ side of the road.

options.text: Either side
Center
Right
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Right
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded and allows you to stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt fastened. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and placing your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: You are driving in the center lane of an expressway and are being passed on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On a highway with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes. Use the left lane only for passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic flow, use the right lane.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, how can you avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: On an interstate, watch for upcoming on-ramps. When it is safe, move to the left lane. This gives vehicles room to enter from the right-hand on-ramp.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Speed up faster than the other traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to the same speed as freeway traffic. This helps you blend in safely. Vehicles entering the freeway must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is also hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always be alert around motorcycles.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set your parking brake and turn your wheels away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: When passing a bicycle, drivers must provide at least ____ of space.

options.text: One foot
Two feet
Three feet
Five feet

questions.correctAnswerText: Three feet
questions.explanation: By law, you must give at least three feet of space when passing a bicycle. Keep this distance until you are completely past the bicycle.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It may be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be fixed in one place or moving (like striping, mowing, or snow removal). They are marked with orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers near schools. It tells you to slow down, drive carefully, and look for children.

questions.question: When must you give the right-of-way to pedestrians?

options.text: When they are in a marked crosswalk.
When they are in any crosswalk or intersection.
When they are crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When they are crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, yield the right-of-way to anyone crossing any street.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on an unpaved county road if no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 40 miles per hour.
45 miles per hour.
50 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: The normal speed limit on an unpaved county road is 50 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection ahead. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the red light.
Slow down and carefully drive through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke covering the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: Slow down right away. Move as far right as you can and stop off the roadway. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Heavy smoke can harm your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: The Child Passenger Restraint Law says all children up to age ____ must use an approved child safety seat.

options.text: Four
Six
Eight

questions.correctAnswerText: Six
questions.explanation: Children up to age six must sit in an approved child safety seat when riding in a moving vehicle.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the center line.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look briefly toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then look ahead again to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Wet or icy roads increase stopping distance. Loose gravel or stones also increase stopping distance.
